description: Burst or broken pipe causing active water discharge inside the building. May cause ceiling damage, flooding, soaked flooring, or structural risk. Requires immediate emergency response.

Water intrusion through the roof, typically occurring during or after heavy rain. May drip into occupied spaces, server rooms, or sensitive equipment areas. Requires temporary patching and roofer dispatch.
Clogged drain, overflowing toilet, or blocked sink fixture causing standing water or sewage backup. Non-emergency unless overflow is spreading to adjacent areas.
Complete or partial loss of electrical power in a zone, floor, or suite. May be caused by tripped breaker, panel fault, or utility failure. Requires licensed electrician or utility contact.
Flickering, buzzing, or non-functional light fixtures in a specific room or area. Typically a bulb, ballast, or fixture issue. Non-emergency unless accompanied by burning smell or sparks.
Visible sparks, burning smell, exposed wiring, or water near electrical outlets creating an immediate fire or electrocution risk. Treat as Critical. May require evacuation and utility shutoff.

Elevator stalled between floors with one or more passengers trapped inside. Emergency phone may or may not be functional. Requires immediate 911 dispatch, elevator service company, and building manager notification.

Elevator not responding, skipping floors, doors not closing properly, or error codes displayed, but no passengers are trapped. Requires elevator service company dispatch. Take elevator out of service until repaired.

Air conditioning system blowing warm or ambient air despite thermostat being set to cool. Room temperature significantly elevated. May be compressor, refrigerant, or controls issue. Priority dispatch if tenant-occupied.
Heating system not producing warm air during cold weather. Thermostat set to heat but room remains cold. May be furnace, boiler, or controls issue. Priority in extreme cold weather.
Unusual sounds from HVAC unit including banging, rattling, grinding, or hissing that indicate mechanical wear or component failure. Schedule inspection before failure worsens.

Fire-rated door not latching, closing, or sealing properly. Critical life-safety issue as fire doors must self-close to contain smoke and flames. Requires priority repair; door should be manually held closed if possible.

Glass door, storefront, or entry door physically damaged, smashed, or shattered. Creates immediate safety hazard from glass and security vulnerability. Requires boarding, glass repair, and possible police report.
Electronic door locks, card readers, or key fobs not functioning. May result in tenants locked out or, more critically, a security door remaining open. Requires access control technician.
Restroom consumable supplies (soap, paper towels, toilet paper) depleted or dispensers jammed. Non-urgent; schedule for next cleaning crew visit.
Carpet stain, spill, or general soiling requiring professional steam cleaning or spot treatment. Non-urgent unless spill is spreading or creating slip hazard.
Bodily fluid, blood, or other biohazardous material requiring specialized cleanup per OSHA standards. Do not allow standard janitorial staff to clean without proper PPE and training.

Strong smell of natural gas, rotten eggs, or sulfur indicating a potential gas leak. Immediate life-safety emergency. Initiate full evacuation, call 911 and gas company, and do not use electrical switches.

Fire alarm triggered or sprinkler system discharged. May be a true fire, smoke event, or false alarm from steam/dust. Requires evacuation, fire department notification, and inspection before re-occupancy.

Visible cracks in walls, floors, or ceilings suggesting structural compromise. Sagging ceilings, fallen ceiling tiles, or partial collapse. Requires structural engineer assessment and possible area evacuation.
Sighting of rodents, insects (cockroaches, ants, bedbugs), or other pests in occupied areas. Requires licensed pest control vendor. Document sighting location and time.
